title: Roll store-bought crescent dough to an even 1/8 inch with a spacer-ring rolling pin
instruction: Roll this crescent dough out to an even 1/8 inch (3.2 mm) thick, then set the rolling pin down off the dough.
context: Rolling dough out flat with a rolling pin, for a pie crust, cookies or a pizza base, is a common home-baking job; the dough here is a store-bought refrigerated one (Pillsbury Original Crescent, an 8 oz can). Spacer rings that slip onto a rolling pin are sold by ordinary kitchen retailers for an even thickness. The rings set it only while both ride on the board, so the pin has to be kept level along its length: with one end lifted it leaves a wedge, thick on that side. A light press springs back; passes past the dough's yield thin it a little each time, so it takes several. An uneven sheet bakes unevenly, browning where it is thin before it is done where it is thick.
setup: Positions are in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, with x forward, y to the robot's left and the table top at z 0. Full scale. A maple board (mid brown, darker than the table; the J.K. Adams Williston board, 16 x 12 x 3/4 inch, modeled 30 cm deep (x) by 40 cm across (y) and 1.9 cm thick) lies fixed on the table, spanning x 10 to 40 and y -20 to 20, top at z 1.9. On it lies a sheet of Pillsbury Original Crescent dough (one 8 oz can, at room temperature, balled, rolled between two 3/16 inch guide strips and trimmed): 11.5 cm (x) by 24 cm (y), 4.8 mm thick (132.5 mL), centered at x 24, y 0. The start sheet is set by this protocol, not by the package. Behind it a handled maple rolling pin (12 inch barrel, as the Frieling Classic with Handles: 53.3 cm overall, 0.73 kg) lies on its rings on the board with its axis along y at x 35, z 5.27: a barrel 6.1 cm across and 30.5 cm long (y -15.25 to 15.25), a silicone 1/8 inch spacer ring 6.74 cm across (3.2 mm proud of the barrel) and 1.5 cm wide on each end of the barrel (|y| 13.75 to 15.25, outside the dough's sides), and dark wooden handles 2.5 cm across and 11.4 cm long (|y| 15.25 to 26.65), reaching past the board's sides without touching anything. The real barrel turns on its bushings, so its rings roll on the board; the sim's pin, one rigid body held by its handles, rides on its rings along the board on a low sliding friction (0.25 static, 0.20 dynamic, the low end of wood on wood, Serway and Jewett Table 5.1) in place of that rolling. The dough is modeled: it has no collider, and is shown as one golden sheet of abutting 2 cm slabs, each as thick as the dough there. It resists the pin (README): it springs back from light presses and flows at 13 kPa once pressed past its yield, the value at which the sim's first pass carries the force of a hand check on this dough (re-balled, rolled with an unringed pin on a cutting board on a kitchen scale at the normal working pressure that keeps dough flat: about 3.0 to 3.5 kg at its peak); at 13 kPa that pass takes 30.4 N (3.1 kg). Real trials (README, Real-world evaluation) use off-the-shelf tools only. One can serves a session: brought to room temperature (20 to 24 C) for 40 minutes before the first trial. Before each trial the dough (the can's dough, or the last rolled sheet balled with its trimmings) is rolled out in all directions to a rough rectangle a little over 12 x 25 cm, then along x with the pin riding two 3/16 inch basswood guide strips (Midwest Products 4059) to 4.76 mm, the strips removed, and trimmed to 11.5 x 24.0 cm with a straightedge (Johnson 40-0564) and a pizza wheel along tape ticks on the board's edge faces (each edge within 3 mm); a caliper reads 4.6 to 5.0 mm at 3 points. The board is taped down inside tape marks (within 2 mm, level within 0.5 degree); the rolling pin and the board are lightly floured. The pin is laid on its x 35 ticks (within 5 mm); its rings are checked once per session at 3.2 mm within 0.1 mm. People handling the dough wear AMMEX X3 nitrile gloves; the dough is never eaten (raw flour and raw dough can carry harmful bacteria, FDA and CDC) and is thrown away at the end of the session. Each gripper finger's pad and tip and each palm face is covered with one layer of Glad Press'n Seal food wrap, fresh every trial, with a red tape band round each fingertip so the overhead video shows the fingers; after each trial the covers are thrown away and the pads and palms wiped with a dry cloth and inspected by eye. The grip through the wrap is checked once per rig by lifting the pin 10 cm by its handles and shaking it 5 s.
scoring: Thickness is read at local points in six 2 cm bands along x centered 3, 7 and 11 cm either side of the board's center line: in each band at row points every 4 cm along x from 1 cm behind the board's front edge (x 11, 15, 19, ... cm) that the dough covers, and at two end points 1 cm inside the band's rolled ends, so an unrolled end counts (a row point within 2 cm of an end point is left to it; no points overlap; 30 on the demo's sheet). The sim reads the one slice under each point. The sheet is on spec when at least 90 % of the points are 3.2 mm (1/8 inch, the rings' gap) within 0.3 mm. It is even when the bands' average thicknesses are within 0.3 mm of each other. All the dough must still be on the board (every edge inside the board's edges, seen on the after photo). The pin is put away when it lies on its rings on the board or table, level within 3 degrees (rings within 5 mm of the surface), its barrel at least 1 cm clear of the dough, and let go (no part of the arms touching it: in the sim their real shapes overlapping it). The trial scores 1.0 when the sheet is on spec, even and on the board and the pin is put away, held for 1 s. It scores 0.5 when at least 90 % of the points are at most 3.7 mm but the sheet is not finished (about one pass left, or a slight wedge), or when the sheet is finished but the pin is not put away (held, left on the dough, or not set down). It scores 0.25 when at least 90 % of the points are at most 4.2 mm and the sheet is even, one level pass from the 4.8 mm start. Otherwise it scores 0 (doing nothing, a single stroke, a wedge, dough pushed off the board). Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0. The arms' end pose, the sheet's length and the hands are free: one or two hands may roll, and the dough thins only where the pin's load passes its yield, in the sim and on the board. Real trial: within 5 minutes of the pin's set-down, each point (the sim's, located with a steel tape) is read with the depth rod of a Neiko 01407A digital caliper (0.01 mm): the rod pushed through the dough to the board, the beam's end face (its footprint, measured once) lowered until it just touches the dough around the point, with the hand holding the caliper's weight. Checks: 0.00 on the bare board, a feeler-leaf stack within 0.03 mm of its recorded value, three re-reads within 0.05 mm. A point under 2.9 mm or a spot where dough stuck to the pin counts as off spec, since a ringed pin stops at 3.2 mm; a hole or tear seen on the after photo (taken before the rod goes in) caps the score at 0.5. The pin is checked with a phone level app and a steel tape, and the overhead video's last second for a finger on it (red tape bands mark the fingertips).
reset_notes: One can of Pillsbury Original Crescent dough serves the session, brought to room temperature for 40 minutes before the first trial. After each trial the rolled sheet is balled up with its trimmings and re-formed: rolled out in all directions to a rough rectangle a little over 12 x 25 cm, then along x with the pin riding two 3/16 inch guide strips (Midwest Products 4059 basswood, 4.76 mm), then trimmed to 11.5 x 24.0 cm with the straightedge and a pizza wheel along the edge ticks (within 3 mm); the caliper reads 4.6 to 5.0 mm at 3 points, or it is rolled again. Scrape the board, brush the pin's barrel and rings, then lightly flour the rolling pin and the board. Lay the pin on its rings at x 35 (within 5 mm). Throw the used gripper covers away, wipe each pad, tip and palm with a dry cloth, inspect them by eye, and fit fresh Glad Press'n Seal covers. Handlers wear AMMEX X3 nitrile gloves.
fidelity: The dough is a model (doughkit) with no collider: the pin rides on its rings and the barrel's contact sets the load. The dough springs back from light presses and thins once pressed past its yield, volume kept, lengthening with its width held. It pushes the pin up and back (13 kPa, from a hand check: 30.4 N on the first pass). The sim's sheet is whole by construction.
scores: Demo: 1.0 (1,420 steps) on task.py 6d12ed359a95. Dream-1 run: 0 (2,400 steps) on the earlier task.py a8f7b3ef9491; not yet re-run.
